title: Quantum states with the same entanglement and local unitary equivalence
abstract: Local operations assisted by classical communication (LOCC) play a fundamental role in the resource-theoretic formulation of entanglement theory inducing an operationally meaningful ordering in the set of entangled states. The particular class within LOCC of local unitary (LU) transformations is obviously closed under inversion. Thus, LU-equivalent states are interconvertible by LOCC and have therefore the same entanglement. For this reason LU-equivalence has been thoroughly studied in the context of entanglement theory. However, as I note here with a simple example, the converse is not true: there exist entangled states that are interconvertible by LOCC but which are not LU-equivalent. This motivates studying under which conditions LOCC interconvertibility is characterized by LU-equivalence. I provide a sufficient condition for this to hold. When one considers multipartite states with full entanglement dimensionality (as quantified by the Schmidt number vector) LOCC interconvertibility can only hold under LU-equivalence.
summary: This paper tackles the relationship between two notions of state equivalence: LOCC-interconvertibility and Local Unitary (LU) equivalence. It proves that for highly entangled multipartite states (those with full entanglement dimensionality), these two concepts coincide. This provides a powerful, sufficient condition for when operational indistinguishability implies a simpler, unitary-based equivalence.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which LOCC-interconvertibility of quantum states implies Local Unitary (LU) equivalence, as this implication is not generally true.
main_result: For multipartite quantum states that possess full entanglement dimensionality (quantified by the Schmidt number vector), LOCC interconvertibility is proven to be equivalent to LU-equivalence.
method: The proof strategy involves using properties of entanglement measures (like entropy) and contradiction, showing that if the states are interconvertible but not LU-equivalent, an inequality must arise contradicting the assumed equality of entanglement measures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on multipartite quantum systems ($ho \in \mathcal{D}_n(d)$) involving $n$ parties, each with local dimension $d \ge 2$. The analysis uses density matrices and concepts derived from entanglement theory.
key_observables: Entanglement of Formation, Schmidt number vector (SNV), and various entanglement entropy measures ($E_j$).
important_parameters: The condition of 'full entanglement dimensionality' ($	ext{SNV}(ho) = (d, \dots, d)$) is the critical parameter regime where the equivalence holds.
main_assumptions: The main result is conditional on the states having full entanglement dimensionality; the general case for mixed states remains open.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the known implication (LU $\implies$ LOCC) and then focuses on finding sufficient conditions for the converse (LOCC $\implies$ LU). The core result is presented in Section IV, proving equivalence under the full entanglement dimensionality condition.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical criterion (full entanglement dimensionality) that simplifies the complex operational question of entanglement equivalence, which is crucial for understanding resource theories in quantum information.
